stem: A burn is red, moist, very painful, and blistered and extends through the epidermis into the superficial dermis. How should the nurse classify it?

options.C: Unclassifiable burn because blistering does not help estimate depth

rationale: Superficial partial-thickness burns involve the epidermis and superficial dermis and characteristically are red, painful, moist, blanching, and blistered. Superficial epidermal burns do not blister, while full-thickness burns extend through the dermis and may have little or no pain. B is correct.
educational_objective: Classify a superficial partial-thickness burn from its tissue depth and characteristic appearance.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
source_locator: Partial-Thickness Burns — superficial partial-thickness burn affects superficial dermis; blisters are common; red/pink and painful
source_claim_supported: Superficial partial-thickness burns extend into the superficial dermis, commonly blister, and are painful/red; superficial burns involve epidermis only and do not blister.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation — burns and tissue injury

source_original.stem: A nurse is classifying a client's burn injury. A burn involving the epidermis and part of the dermis, presenting with blistering, redness, and significant pain, would be classified as:

options.B: Partial-thickness burn with blistering and significant pain
options.C: A burn with no clinical classification system available
options.D: Superficial (first-degree) burn affecting only the epidermis

source_original.rationale: A partial-thickness (second-degree) burn involves the epidermis and part of the dermis, characteristically presenting with blistering, redness, and significant pain (since nerve endings remain intact), distinct from superficial (first-degree) burns (epidermis only, no blistering) and full-thickness (third-degree) burns (through the full dermis, often with reduced pain due to nerve destruction).
source_original.source_detail: Burn depth: partial-thickness injury extends into dermis and commonly blisters and is painful; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Specified superficial partial-thickness rather than all partial-thickness burns because deep partial-thickness burns can have reduced pain. Replaced a generic organization homepage with an exact NCBI burn-classification locator.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Superficial partial-thickness features and distinctions from superficial/full-thickness burns are directly supported.

distractor_audit.A: Depth and pain/blister pattern are inconsistent with full thickness.
distractor_audit.B: Exact match for superficial partial thickness.
distractor_audit.C: Burn depth has standard clinical classification.
distractor_audit.D: Superficial burns involve epidermis only and typically do not blister.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Specifying superficial dermis/red-moist-painful-blistered removes ambiguity with deep partial-thickness burns.
audit_findings.cueing: Stem uses clinical morphology rather than naming second degree.
audit_findings.blueprint: Burn complications/tissue injury fit Physiological Adaptation.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked NCBI Burn Classification; B remains uniquely correct.
